summary: SDK sidecar queueing causes delayed funcall ACKs and stale 'at-most-once' semantics
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated cases where function/tool calls issued from a streaming session are executed twice downstream but the SDK reports a single ACK, or conversely the downstream reports a single execution while the SDK never receives an ACK. Impact: BrightAssist is observing duplicated side-effects (duplicate webhook posts and duplicate DB writes) in some long-running streaming sessions and in other sessions a missing ack leads to 'at-most-once' semantics that drop retries.

Impact:
- Duplicate downstream side-effects in ~0.4% of streaming sessions for this customer (dedicated pool).
- Some long-lived sessions (>10 minutes) silently transition to stalled ACK behavior and do not surface retries to caller.
- Business impact: duplicate notifications to end users, billing disputes, and increased operational load on customer infra.

Environment:
- Customer: BrightAssist.ai (dedicated cluster, pinned model version).
- SDK: Typescript streaming client v1.6.2 using local sidecar proxy (edge sidecar pattern).
- Sidecar: redwood/sdk-proxy v0.9.1 configured with local queueing and backpressure window of 30s.
- Platform: Redwood Dedicated (us-east), serving-runtime 2026-02-28 build.

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Start a long-lived streaming chat session via TS SDK with function/tool enabled.
2) Trigger a chain of funcalls that produce webhook POSTs to customer's HTTP endpoint (external).
3) Simulate brief spikes in throughput or deliberately throttle the external endpoint for 20–40s.
4) Observe: in ~1 out of 250 sessions a) downstream receives duplicate webhook posts OR b) downstream only receives post but SDK never surfaces ACK and client retries are suppressed.

Expected behavior:
- Each funcall should be at-most-once delivered to external webhook when idempotency keys are provided, and SDK should always surface explicit ACK/confirmation for each funcall to the client layer so retriable semantics are correct.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate downstream executions in some sessions despite SDK indicating single ack.
- Other sessions show the external webhook executed once but the SDK's per-action ack state is stale (no ack), leading to client-level retry attempts that are suppressed by sidecar queue dedup logic.

Logs / Traces provided by customer (redacted):
- SDK trace id: trace-bruise-4821 (attached log excerpt).
- Sidecar queue snapshots show enqueue timestamp + dequeue > 25s for implicated requests.
- External webhook logs show two POSTs with identical idempotency header within 4s window for duplicates.

Temporary workaround used by customer:
- Increased sidecar backpressure window to 90s and disabled local dedup for funcalls. This reduced duplicates but caused higher retry noise and request timeouts elsewhere.

Investigation notes (support + eng):
- Hypothesis 1: Sidecar's local queueing implementation splits a funcall message into two enqueued chunks after an internal reconnect, causing the serving runtime to accept both chunks and execute twice while only one ACK path is propagated back to the SDK client.
- Hypothesis 2: A race between the sidecar's dedup index eviction (TTL-based) and the SDK's per-action ack state means the SDK marks action as acked locally while the sidecar replays the request after connection migration, producing duplicate downstream side-effects.
- Evidence: Correlated occurrences at times of sidecar reconnects and when queue dequeue latency exceeds configured threshold. Linked trace shows one successful POST followed by an immediate replay from a different connection id.
- Reproducibility: Intermittent; reproduces with deterministic steps when artificially throttling external endpoint and forcing sidecar reconnects via TCP kill.

Work performed so far:
- Collected SDK and sidecar debug logs from customer (attached).
- Replayed traces in staging with similar sidecar version and reproduced duplicate POSTs under forced reconnects.
- Created repro harness in internal staging and opened PR to add additional correlation headers in sidecar for debugging (see related_github_prs).

Next steps / proposed fix:
- Short term: recommend BrightAssist keep dedup disabled on sidecar and use server-side idempotency verification (idempotency-token validation at webhook endpoint) until fix lands.
- Medium term: update sidecar to attach persistent per-action nonce and carry original connection id in replayed messages; ensure runtime only executes funcall once per persistent nonce and surfaces ACK on all in-flight client connections.
- Long term: add end-to-end instrumentation (per-action lifecycle spans) surfaced in Console to make ACK vs execution visible to customers.

Owner / escalation path:
- Assigned eng owner: Marco Chen (serving-runtime / sidecar).
- Support contact: Aisha Patel (CS lead for BrightAssist).

2026-03-11 - Marco Chen (engineer): Narrowed repro to sidecar enqueue/dequeue path. Added additional correlation headers in staging PR for more visibility. Refer to PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-proxy/pull/812.
2026-03-12 - BrightAssist (customer): Confirmed temporary config change reduced dupes but lament higher latency. Requesting ETA on patch and guidance to avoid data-loss while patch is pending.
2026-03-12 - Marco Chen: Proposed plan to ship sidecar v0.9.2 with nonce propagation and strengthened dedup. Target release 2026-03-18 subject to QA. Will notify customer and add migration guide.

resolution: Fix in progress: sidecar nonce propagation patch merged to staging; release to prod scheduled pending QA. Customer recommended to enable server-side idempotency checks and keep sidecar dedup disabled until release.
